title: Little Office of the Most Holy Name of Jesus
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: In nomine Jesu omne genu flectatur, coelestium, terrestrium et infernorum.
blocks.english: At the name of Jesus every knee shall bow, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine, labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus, in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine, ad adjuvandum me festina.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

blocks.source: Gloria Patri et Filio et Spiritui Sancto, etc. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. vel Laus tibi Domine, rex aeternae gloriae.
blocks.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost, etc. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Or Praise be to Thee, O Lord, King of everlasting glory.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Jesu dulcis memoria; Dans vera cordis gaudia, Sed super mel et omnia; Ejus dulcis praesentia.
blocks.english:
Sweet is the remembrance of Jesus,
Giving true joys to the heart;
But sweeter than honey and all things
Is His sweet presence.

blocks.source: Nil canitur suavius; Nil auditur jucundius, Nil cogitatur dulcius; Quam Jesus, Dei Filius.
blocks.english:
Nothing sweeter is sung,
Nothing more pleasing is heard,
Nothing more delightful is thought of
Than Jesus, the Son of God.

blocks.source: Jesu, spes poenitentibus; Quam pius es petentibus! Quam bonus te quaerentibus! Sed quid Invenientibus?
blocks.english:
Jesus, hope of the penitent,
How loving Thou art to those who ask!
How good to those who seek Thee!
But what art Thou to those who find Thee?

blocks.source: Jesu, dulcedo cordium; Fons vivus, lumen mentium, Excedens omne gaudium; Et omne desiderium.
blocks.english:
Jesus, sweetness of hearts,
Living fountain, light of minds,
Surpassing every joy
And every desire.

blocks.source: Nec lingua valet dicere; Nec littera exprimere, Expertus potest credere; Quid sit Jesum diligere.
blocks.english:
No tongue can tell,
No writing can express;
One who has experienced it can believe
What it is to love Jesus.

blocks.source: Jesum quaeram in lectulo; Clauso cordis cubiculo, Privatim et in publico; Quaeram amore sedulo.
blocks.english:
I shall seek Jesus upon my bed,
In the closed chamber of my heart;
In private and in public
I shall seek Him with diligent love.

blocks.source: ℣. Sit nomen Domini benedictum.
blocks.english: ℣. Blessed be the name of the Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Ex hoc nunc et usque in saeculum.
blocks.english: ℟. From henceforth, now and for ever.

blocks.source: Ant. Vocatum est nomen ejus Jesus, quod vocatum est ab Angelo, priusquam in utero conciperetur: sanctum et terribile nomen ejus.
blocks.english: Ant. His name was called Jesus, the name given by the Angel before He was conceived in the womb: holy and terrible is His name.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine, exaudi orationem meam.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Sancti nominis tui, Domine, timorem pariter et amorem fac nos habere perpetuum; quia nunquam tua gubernatione destituis, quos in soliditate tuae dilectionis instituis. Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate Spiritus Sancti Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum.
blocks.english: Grant us, O Lord, a lasting fear and love alike of Thy holy Name; for Thou never withdrawest Thy governance from those whom Thou establishest in the steadfastness of Thy love. Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

blocks.source: ℟. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. Amen.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Cum Maria diluculo; Jesum quaeram in tumulo, Clamore cordis querulo; Mente quaeram, non oculo.
blocks.english:
With Mary at the break of day
I shall seek Jesus in the tomb;
With the plaintive cry of my heart
I shall seek with the mind, not with the eye.

blocks.source: Tumbam perfundam fletibus; Locum replens gemitibus: Jesu provolar pedibus; Strictis haerens amplexibus.
blocks.english:
I shall drench the tomb with tears,
Filling the place with groans;
I shall fall at the feet of Jesus,
Clinging to Him in close embraces.

blocks.source: Jesu rex admirabilis; Et triumphator nobilis, Dulcedo ineffabilis; Totus desiderabilis.
blocks.english:
Jesus, wondrous King
And noble conqueror,
Ineffable sweetness,
Wholly to be desired.

blocks.source: Mane nobiscum, Domine; Et nos illustra lumine, Pulsa mentis caligne; Mundum replens dulcedine.
blocks.english:
Abide with us, O Lord,
And enlighten us with Thy light;
Drive away the darkness of the mind,
Filling the world with sweetness.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “caligne”; the translation understands this as caligine, darkness. The printed spelling is retained.

blocks.source: Quando cor nostrum visitas; Tunc lucet ei veritas, Mundi vilescit vanitas, Et intus fervet caritas.
blocks.english:
When Thou visitest our heart,
Then truth shines upon it;
The vanity of the world grows worthless,
And charity burns within.

blocks.source: Amor Jesu dulcissimus; Et vere suavissimus, Plus millies gratissimus; Quam dicere sufficimus.
blocks.english:
The sweetest love of Jesus
Is truly most delightful,
A thousand times more welcome
Than we can adequately tell.

blocks.source: Hoc probat ejus passio; Hoc sanguinis effusio, Per quam nobis redemptio; Datur, et Dei visio.
blocks.english:
His Passion proves this,
And the shedding of His blood,
Through which redemption is given to us
And the vision of God.

blocks.source: ℣. Sit nomen Domini benedictum.
blocks.english: ℣. Blessed be the name of the Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Ex hoc nunc et usque in saeculum.
blocks.english: ℟. From henceforth, now and for ever.

blocks.source: Ant. A solis ortu usque ad occasum laudabile nomen Domini.
blocks.english: Ant. From the rising of the sun unto its setting, the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine, exaudi orationem meam.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: ℟. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. Amen.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Jesum omnes agnoscite; Amorem ejus poscite, Jesum ardenter quaerite; Quaerendo inardescite.
Sic amantem diligite; Amoris vicem reddite, In hunc odorem currite; Et vota votis reddite.
Jesu auctor clementiae; Totius spes laetitiae: Dulcoris fons et gratiae; Verae cordis deliciae.
blocks.english:
Jesus, author of mercy,
Hope of all gladness,
Fountain of sweetness and grace,
True delight of the heart.

blocks.source: Jesu mi bone, sentiam; Amoris tui copiam, Da mihi per praesentiam; Tuam videre gloriam.
blocks.english:
My good Jesus, may I feel
The abundance of Thy love;
By Thy presence grant me
To see Thy glory.

blocks.source: Cum digne loqui nequeam; De Te tamen ne sileam, Amor facit, ut audeam; Cum de Te solum gaudeam.
blocks.english:
Though I cannot speak worthily,
Let me nevertheless not be silent concerning Thee.
Love makes me dare,
Since in Thee alone I rejoice.

blocks.source: Tua, Jesu, dilectio; Grata mentis refectio, Replens sine fastidio; Dans famem desiderio.
blocks.english:
Thy love, O Jesus,
Is the welcome refreshment of the mind,
Filling without weariness,
And giving hunger to desire.

blocks.source: Qui Te gustant, esuriunt; Qui bibunt, adhuc sitiunt, Desiderare nesciunt; Nisi Jesum, quem diligunt.
blocks.english:
Those who taste Thee hunger;
Those who drink still thirst.
They know not how to desire
Anything but Jesus, whom they love.

blocks.source: ℣. Sit nomen Domini benedictum.
blocks.english: ℣. Blessed be the name of the Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Ex hoc nunc et usque in saeculum.
blocks.english: ℟. From henceforth, now and for ever.

blocks.source: Ant. Nec enim aliud nomen est sub coelo datum hominibus, in quo oportet nos salvos fieri.
blocks.english: Ant. For there is no other name under heaven given to men, wherein we must be saved.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine, exaudi orationem meam.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.english: ℟. Amen.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Quocumque loco fuero; Mecum Jesum desidero: Quam laetus, cum invenero! Quam felix, cum tenuero!
blocks.english:
Wherever I may be,
I desire Jesus with me.
How glad I shall be when I find Him!
How blessed when I hold Him!

blocks.source: Jam, quod quaesivi, video; Quod concupivi, teneo, Amore Jesu langueo; Et corde totus ardeo.
blocks.english:
Now I see what I have sought;
I hold what I have longed for.
I languish with love of Jesus,
And burn with all my heart.

blocks.source: Jesus cum sic diligitur; Hic amor non extinguitur; Non tepescit, nec moritur; Plus crescit, et accenditur.
blocks.english:
When Jesus is loved thus,
This love is not extinguished;
It neither grows lukewarm nor dies,
But grows and is kindled still more.

blocks.source: Hic amor ardet jugiter; Dulcescit mirabiliter, Sapit delectabiliter; Delectat et feliciter.
blocks.english:
This love burns continually;
It grows wondrously sweet,
It tastes delightful,
And brings blessed delight.

blocks.source: Hic amor missus coelitus; Haeret mihi medullitus, Mentem incendit penitus; Hoc delectatur spiritus.
O beatum incendium; Et ardens desiderium, O dulce refrigerium; Amare Dei Filium!
blocks.english:
O blessed fire
And burning desire!
O sweet refreshment,
To love the Son of God!

blocks.source: ℣. Sit nomen Domini benedictum.
blocks.english: ℣. Blessed be the name of the Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Ex hoc nunc et usque in saeculum.
blocks.english: ℟. From henceforth, now and for ever.

blocks.source: Ant. Memores erunt nominis tui, Domine, in omni generatione et generationem.
blocks.english: Ant. They shall remember Thy name, O Lord, throughout every generation.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine, exaudi orationem meam.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.english: ℟. Amen.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Jesu, flos matris virginis; Amor nostrae dulcedinis, Tibi laus, honor numinis; Regnum beatitudinis!
blocks.english:
Jesus, flower of the Virgin Mother,
Love of our sweetness,
To Thee be praise, divine honour,
And the kingdom of blessedness!

blocks.source: Veni, veni, rex optime; Pater immensae gloriae, Affulge menti clarius; Jam exspectatus saepius.
blocks.english:
Come, come, most excellent King,
Father of boundless glory;
Shine more brightly upon the mind,
Thou who hast already been awaited so often.

blocks.source: Jesu sole serenior; Et balsamo suavior, Omni dulcore dulcior; Prae cunctis amabilior.
blocks.english:
Jesus, brighter than the sun,
Sweeter than balsam,
Sweeter than every sweetness,
More lovable than all things.

blocks.source: Cujus gustus sic afficit; Cujus odor sic reficit, In quo mens mea deficit; Solus amanti sufficit.
Tu mentis delectatio; Amoris consummatio, Tu mea gloriatio; Jesu, mundi salvatio:
blocks.english:
Thou art the delight of the mind,
The consummation of love;
Thou art my glory,
Jesus, salvation of the world.

blocks.source: Dilecte mi, revertere; Consors paternae dexterae, Hostem vicisti prospere; Jam coeli regno fruere.
blocks.english:
My Beloved, return,
Thou who sharest the Father’s right hand.
Thou hast gloriously vanquished the enemy;
Now enjoy the kingdom of heaven.

blocks.source: Sequar Te, quoquo ieris; Mihi tolli non poteris, Cum meum cor abstuleris; Jesu, laus nostri generis.
blocks.english:
I shall follow Thee wherever Thou goest.
Thou canst not be taken away from me,
Since Thou hast carried off my heart,
Jesus, glory of our race.

blocks.source: ℣. Sit nomen Domini benedictum.
blocks.english: ℣. Blessed be the name of the Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Ex hoc nunc et usque in saeculum.
blocks.english: ℟. From henceforth, now and for ever.

blocks.source: Ant. Fecit mihi magna, qui potens est, et sanctum nomen ejus.
blocks.english: Ant. He who is mighty hath done great things for me, and holy is His name.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine, exaudi orationem meam.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Coeli cives, occurrite; Portas vestras attolite, Triumphatori dicite: Ave Jesus, rex inclyte!
Rex virtutum, rex gloriae; Rex insignis victoriae, Jesu, largitor vaniae; Honor coelestis curiae.
blocks.english:
King of powers, King of glory,
King of splendid victory,
Jesus, giver of pardon,
Honour of the heavenly court.
blocks.editorialNote: Printed comparison edition, not certification of the cited office edition. The printed reading is “Jesu largitor veniae, honor caelestis curiae.”. The attached Latin is retained; prepared English follows the documented reading where it differs.

sourceReading.reading: Jesu largitor veniae, honor caelestis curiae.
sourceReading.attachedReading: Jesu, largitor vaniae; Honor coelestis curiae.

blocks.source: Tu fons misericordiae; Tu verae lumen patriae, Pelle nubem tristitiae; Dans nobis lucem gloriae.
blocks.english:
Thou art the fountain of mercy,
The light of our true homeland.
Drive away the cloud of sadness,
Giving us the light of glory.

blocks.source: Te coeli chorus praedicat; Et tuas laudes replicat, Jesus orbem laetificat; Et nos Deo pacificat.
blocks.english:
The choir of heaven proclaims Thee
And repeats Thy praises;
Jesus makes the world rejoice
And reconciles us to God.

blocks.source: Jesus in pace imperat; Quae omnem sensum superat: Hanc mea mens desiderat; Et ea frui properat.
blocks.english:
Jesus reigns in peace
Which surpasses all understanding.
My mind desires this peace
And hastens to enjoy it.

blocks.source: Jesus ad Patrem rediit; Coeleste regnum subiit, Cor meum a me transiit; Post Jesum simul abiit.
blocks.english:
Jesus has returned to the Father
And entered the heavenly kingdom.
My heart has passed away from me
And gone at once after Jesus.

blocks.source: Quem prosequamur laudibus; Votis, hymnis et precibus, Ut nos donet coelestibus; Cum ipso frui sedibus.
blocks.english:
Let us accompany Him with praises,
Vows, hymns, and prayers,
That He may grant us to enjoy
The heavenly dwelling with Him.

blocks.source: ℣. Sit nomen Domini benedictum.
blocks.english: ℣. Blessed be the name of the Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Ex hoc nunc et usque in saeculum.
blocks.english: ℟. From henceforth, now and for ever.

blocks.source: Ant. Omne quodcumque facitis in verbo, aut in opere, omnia in nomine Domini Jesu Christi facite, gratias agentes Deo, et Patri per ipsum.
blocks.english: Ant. Whatsoever ye do in word or in deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God and the Father through Him.

blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.english: ℟. Amen.

blocks.source: Salve Jesu, Jesu pie; Fili Dei et Mariae, Quem de Patre sine matre; Et de Matre sine patre, Natum credo firmiter.
blocks.english:
Hail, Jesus, loving Jesus,
Son of God and of Mary,
Whom I firmly believe to be born
Of the Father without a mother,
And of the Mother without a father.

blocks.source: Sana me, et sanus ero; Et sanabis hic, ut spero, Sic in coelo Te videre; Cum Beatis possidere, Gaudeam perenniter.
blocks.english:
Heal me, and I shall be healed;
And Thou wilt heal me here, as I hope,
So that in heaven I may rejoice for ever
To see Thee
And possess Thee with the blessed.

editorialNotes.text: All five pages have been visually compared. English is prepared from this Latin edition, and hymn fragments split by columns or pages are joined into their complete stanzas. Only the six hours printed in the source are offered: Matins, Prime, Terce, None, Vespers, and Compline. The printed Ordinaria remains available separately as the common opening; no missing Lauds or Sext is supplied. One malformed word at Compline has explicitly provisional English.
